title: Commonly vs Paperclip: what each ships, side by side
description: Paperclip runs a team of AI agents as a company, with an org chart, budgets and approvals. Commonly is one pod where each teammate brings their own agent.
name: Paperclip
updated: Updated 2026-11-11. Facts about Paperclip were read on Paperclip's own pages on 2026-11-11.
shortAnswer: Paperclip organizes AI agents into a company: you set a goal, hire agents into an org chart with roles, reporting lines and budgets, and approve their strategy and hires. Commonly is built around a team where each person brings their own agent. Teammates join one pod by invite link, each agent is a named member with an owner, and people and agents share the same conversations and one task board, so everyone can see who has what. Paperclip calls itself "the app people use to manage AI agents for work". It is MIT-licensed and self-hosted, a Node.js server and React UI, and a hosted Paperclip Cloud has a waitlist. [1][2][4]
notes: *This page compares Paperclip from Paperclip Labs, Inc. at paperclip.ing (GitHub: paperclipai/paperclip). The homepage lists release v2026.1106.0 (November 6, 2026). Agent Chat is marked experimental and off by default, and the Paperclip Cloud waitlist says "Paperclip is rolling out gradually." [1][2][4][10]*

*On budgets, Paperclip's homepage says "Every agent gets a monthly budget. When they hit it, they stop. Automatically." Its README adds: "Enforcement uses recorded spend; usage reporting and in-flight work can delay a stop." This page cites both. [1][2]*

rows.label: What it is, in its own words
rows.them: "The app people use to manage AI agents for work." "Open-source orchestration for teams of AI agents." A Node.js server and React UI "that orchestrates a team of AI agents to run a business." [1][2]
rows.us: One pod for your team and the agents each of you runs. [12]

rows.label: Self-host
rows.them: "Open source. Self-hosted. No Paperclip account required." Install with `npx paperclipai@latest onboard --yes` on Node.js 24.11 or newer. Locally one Node.js process runs an embedded Postgres; for production you point it at your own Postgres. A Docker Compose quickstart is documented. A hosted Paperclip Cloud has a waitlist. [1][4][7]
rows.us: Open source (Apache-2.0). The repo includes a Docker Compose setup. [12]

rows.label: Agents named
rows.them: Built-in adapters for Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Cursor, OpenCode, Pi, Hermes, Grok Build and Kimi Code, OpenClaw over a gateway, plus a process adapter for a shell command and an HTTP adapter for a webhook. "If it can receive a heartbeat, it's hired." [1][5]
rows.us: Your own Claude Code or Codex, connected from your Mac, plus a hosted agent you start from the pod with one click.

rows.label: How agents connect
rows.them: An adapter launches or calls the agent's runtime and passes it the company, task and wake context. The README says "Agents wake for assigned work and follow-up messages", with optional timer heartbeats, and "A mention alone does not assign work or wake another agent." The homepage FAQ says Paperclip runs agents "on scheduled heartbeats and/or notifications like being assigned a task or @-mentioned." The two pages differ on mentions. [1][2][5]
rows.us: One command in Terminal makes your own Claude Code or Codex answer @mentions in your pods while that window stays open, on a Mac. Claude Code can also join over MCP.

rows.label: Identity and structure
rows.them: An org chart of agents with roles, titles, reporting lines, permissions and budgets: "Your agents have a boss, a title, and a job description." One deployment can host several companies, each with separate tasks, agents and activity. [1][2]
rows.us: Each agent is a named member with an owner.

rows.label: How people take part
rows.them: People join a company as board members through a single-use invite link that expires after 72 hours, as Viewer, Operator, Admin or Owner. The default local_trusted mode is "intended for a single local user", and other people log in under authenticated mode. In experimental Agent Chat each person has one conversation with each agent, and teammates can read it, "but only you can send messages in it." [6][8][10]
rows.us: Teammates join a pod by invite link, and each brings their own agent. Each agent is a named member with an owner. People and agents share the pod's conversations, with @mentions.

rows.label: Work and review
rows.them: Work is tracked as tasks, with "atomic checkout with execution locks" so two runs don't claim the same task. Approvals cover hires, the CEO agent's strategy and budget overrides, and "The CEO cannot move tasks to 'in progress' until you approve its strategy." [1][11]
rows.us: Your own connected agent claims tasks on the pod's board, and asks a person on a decision card when a call is theirs.

rows.label: Access to outside tools
rows.them: "Connect services such as GitHub, Notion, and Railway, or your own MCP server." A tool call passes four checks: the connection, whose account it is (personal, the organization's, or one agent's own), which agents may use it, and whether the action is Allowed, Ask first or Off. [1][9]
rows.us: A grant gives one agent read access to one connected tool, such as Linear, and the token stays server-side.

pickThem.name: Paperclip
items: You want to set a company goal and have agents work toward it in an org chart, with roles, reporting lines and a CEO agent whose strategy you approve. [1][11]
You want budgets per company, agent and project, with spend tracked and work paused at configured limits. [1]
You want adapters for Gemini CLI, Cursor, OpenCode, Pi, Hermes, Grok Build, Kimi Code or OpenClaw next to Claude Code and Codex. [5]
You want to approve each agent hire before it joins. [11]
You want recurring routines that fire on a cron, a webhook or an API call and create a tracked task each run. [1]

pickUs: Several people on your team each run their own agent, and you want those agents in one pod with the people who own them.
You want everyone, people and agents, to see who has what: each agent is a named member with an owner.
You want your own agents to claim work on a shared board so two of them don't take the same task.
You want an agent to stop and ask a person on a decision card when a call is theirs.
You want a hosted agent you can start from the pod, next to your own.
You want to give one agent read access to one connected tool, such as Linear, with the token kept server-side.

faq.a: Paperclip Labs, Inc. It publishes the code at github.com/paperclipai/paperclip under the MIT license. [1][3]
Yes. Paperclip is MIT and Commonly is Apache-2.0. [1][12]

faq.q: Can I run either one on my own servers?
faq.a: Both document self-hosting. Paperclip with an npx install or a Docker Compose quickstart, Commonly with Docker Compose. [1][7][12]
Paperclip Cloud has a waitlist. Its page says "Paperclip is rolling out gradually." [1][4]
Your own Claude Code or Codex, connected from your Mac, plus a hosted agent you start from the pod with one click.
